picks.title: Slay the Spire 2 lead says the 'garbage' placeholder art is important and gen AI would ruin it
picks.excerpt: Slay the Spire 2's lead defends deliberately rough hand-made placeholder art in Early Access, arguing generative AI 'would ruin it' because polished AI fill-ins make players judge an unfinished build as a finished 1.0 — a craft-and-iteration case against gen AI in the art pipeline.
picks.rationale: A concrete craft argument from a shipping studio lead — why rough hand-made placeholders beat polished AI fill-ins during Early Access reframes how designers stage unfinished art; credible GamesRadar+ interview on a fresh, distinct release.

picks.title: iOS developer made a Capybara game using vibe-coding and won $25,000
picks.excerpt: An iOS developer built a Capybara food-delivery game almost entirely by 'vibe-coding' with Claude Code and won a $25,000 prize — a concrete example of AI coding agents collapsing the barrier for a solo creator to ship a finished mobile game.
picks.rationale: Highly actionable proof point — a solo dev shipping and winning $25K on a Claude Code vibe-coded game shows exactly how AI coding agents lower the barrier to finishing a mobile title; distinct outlet keeps the section diverse.

picks.title: MMO life sim Seed's AI-powered avatars prove once again that nothing shatters immersion quicker than crappy chatbot dialogue
picks.excerpt: PC Gamer tries the AI-driven NPCs in the relaunched MMO life sim Seed and finds the generative chatbot dialogue breaks immersion rather than deepening it — a hands-on craft verdict on where real-time LLM avatars still fall short in shipped games.
picks.rationale: The freshest pick and a hands-on reality check — a shipped MMO's real-time LLM avatars breaking immersion tells designers exactly where generative NPC dialogue still fails; third distinct outlet (PC Gamer).

picks.title: Steam study of over 53,000 games finds "60–90% of the growth" in monthly releases is from games using AI and "almost none of them make money"
picks.excerpt: A study of 53,597 Steam titles finds AI-made games now drive 60–90% of the growth in monthly releases yet almost none earn money — hard data on how generative AI is reshaping (and flooding) the storefront where designers' work has to compete for attention.
picks.rationale: Hard data over vibes — a 53,597-title study quantifying how AI games flood Steam yet earn nothing directly shapes how designers weigh AI-scale output against the storefront they must compete in; credible GamesRadar+ report on a distinct study.
